steps.title: The pattern
say: A shock absorber is a queue between bursty producers and steady consumers. It takes the burst at the speed the producer sends it, and the consumers drain it at their own pace.
This tour takes about ten minutes. Each step tells you what to do, waits while you do it, and then explains what you see. Press Continue when you are ready.

steps.title: The ticket sale
say: This is concert ticket sales. When tickets go on sale, fifteen hundred purchase requests arrive in a couple of seconds. Otherwise they trickle in.

Two booking workers reserve seats at a steady twenty a second each. The queue between the On-Sale Page and the workers is the shock absorber. It has limits, in space and in time, and the two cards show both.

steps.title: Run it
steps.do: Press Play, at the top of the page under Run it.

expect.note: Not everything is running yet. Play takes a few seconds.

say: Press Play. It creates the queue and its dead message queue, starts the two booking workers, and then the On-Sale Page.
Press Continue when the dots on the diagram are moving.

steps.title: A burst arrives
steps.do: Under Step through it, press Fire a burst now. Or wait: a burst comes every minute.
say: Now watch a burst. Under Step through it, press Fire a burst now, or wait for the next one. The number on the queue jumps to about fifteen hundred within a couple of seconds, and then falls steadily as the two workers book forty a second between them.

steps.title: The producer's side
steps.do: Click logs on the On-Sale Page node.

expect.note: The On-Sale Page log is not open yet.

say: Click logs on the On-Sale Page node. For a burst it says how quickly the requests were handed over, and a few seconds later that the broker confirmed every one: all stored, none refused. While the burst fits in the queue, the page is not slowed down.

steps.title: The consumer's side
steps.do: Click logs on the Booking 1 node.

expect.note: The Booking 1 log is not open yet.

say: Now click logs on the Booking 1 node. It books at its own steady pace, and for a request that waited more than a few seconds it says how long. The workers never see more than they can handle.

steps.title: A burst too big for the queue
steps.do: Open the card The burst is bigger than the queue, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: Now break it. Scroll to Break it, open the card called The burst is bigger than the queue, and press Break it.
A second on-sale page releases six thousand tickets at once: four times the burst the queue was sized for.

steps.title: The limit in space
steps.do: Read that page's log beside the diagram, and watch the number on the queue.
say: The first few thousand requests are stored. Then the broker refuses the rest, one at a time, with the words: Spool Over Quota. The page sums up how many customers got no booking.
A queue absorbs a burst up to its size, and not beyond. Past that, the publisher is told, and has to decide what to do. The size of the absorber is a decision, made from the biggest burst you expect.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: Clear the backlog
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The card is still in effect. Press Reset in the bar at the top.

say: Press Reset. It clears the backlog, which would otherwise take the workers more than a minute.

steps.title: Requests that cannot wait
steps.do: Open the card Requests go stale while they wait, and press Break it.

expect.note: The card is not in effect yet. Open it and press Break it.

say: Now the second limit. Open the card called Requests go stale while they wait, and press Break it.
A second on-sale page releases fifteen hundred tickets whose seat holds lapse after twenty seconds.

steps.title: The limit in time
steps.do: Watch the two queues inside the broker for about half a minute.
say: The burst takes the two workers about forty seconds to get through. So the requests at the back are still waiting when their twenty seconds run out. Watch for half a minute: the broker moves each of those to the dead message queue, and its number climbs.
Absorbing a burst costs time. A request that waits is a request handled late, and a time to live on the message says how late is too late.

expect.note: The card is not in effect, so there is nothing to see yet.

steps.title: Clear both queues
steps.do: Press Reset, in the bar at the top of the page.

expect.note: The card is still in effect. Press Reset in the bar at the top.

say: Press Reset. It clears what is left on the purchase queue, and deletes the expired requests on the dead message queue. Both numbers go back to zero.

steps.title: When to use it
say: That is the shock absorber. Use it when load arrives in spikes, such as a sale or a batch job, that the consumers could not take all at once.
The cost is that work waits. A burst bigger than the queue is refused, and some requests are stale by the time they are handled.
Press Cleanup when you are done, or pick another pattern from the sidebar.
